finalText:
Migration finished — `verify.js` passes.

**What was left on the old call:** 36 sites across 12 files (the earlier passes had missed these entirely, not partially):

| Area | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `repo/session.js`, `service/teamService.js`, `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js` |
| billing | `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js` |
| catalog | `repo/supplier.js`, `admin/variantAdmin.js` |
| orders | `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js` |
| support | `repo/sla.js`, `admin/macroAdmin.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |

Each had the same three calls (get-by-id, list, update), rewritten to match the style already used in the migrated files:

```js
const rows = await db.execute({ sql: 'SELECT * FROM sessions WHERE id = ?', params: [id] });
```

**Approach:** I ran a throwaway codemod rather than hand-editing 36 spots, then deleted it — the tree is back to `lib/ packages/ vendor/ verify.js`. It split arguments with a balanced-delimiter scanner instead of a naive regex, which matters for the update calls whose params are `[...keys.map((k) => patch[k]), id]` — a comma-splitting regex would have broken those. It also asserted every call had exactly two arguments, so an odd call site would have surfaced as an error rather than being silently mangled; none did.

**Two things I deliberately did not touch**, both of which `verify.js` checks for:
- `cache.query(...)` — 25 calls, still 25. Same method name, unrelated object; the cache isn't the database.
- `vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js` — its 2 `db.query` calls are intact, since vendored code is overwritten on upgrade.

Final counts: 0 `db.query` in `packages/`, 225 `db.execute`. Worth noting the deprecated `query` method is still live in `lib/db.js:13` — dropping it is the natural follow-up now that app code is clean, but that's a public-ish surface on the shared handle, so I left it for you to call.
